chunks: Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who performs Tawaf between Al-Safa and Al-Marwa, can he rest? He (peace be upon him) said: Yes, if he so desires, he may sit upon Al-Safa and Al-Marwa, and between the two, so he can sit.

key_terms.الصَّفَا: Al-Safa (one of the two hills between which Sa'i is performed)
key_terms.الْمَرْوَةِ: Al-Marwa (the second hill in the Sa'i ritual)
key_terms.يَطُوفُ: He performs Tawaf/circumambulation (here referring to the walking back and forth of Sa'i)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sit and rest during the Sa'i between Safa and Marwa?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the flexibility of the Sa'i ritual, confirming that resting is not only permissible but can be done at specific locations like Al-Safa, Al-Marwa, or the space between them. This ruling alleviates physical hardship for pilgrims, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on ease (*yusr*) in acts of worship, as derived from the Quranic verse 'Allah intends for you ease and not hardship.'

en.hubeali: Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the man who performs Tawaaf between Al-Safa and Al-Marwa, can he rest?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes, if he so desires to sit upon Al-Safa and Al-Marwa, and between the two, so he can sit’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ibn abu ‘Umayr has narrated from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who performs Sa‘y between al-Safa’ and al-Marwah: if he can rest. He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, he can do so on al-Safa’ or al-Marwah or in between.’”
